Every course in 'courses' is invented for the demo: titles, numbers, credits, offerings, prerequisites and descriptions are illustrative, not catalog facts. A course that is in grinnell_catalog.json always wins over a sample with the same id. 'descriptions' holds mock descriptions, written for the demo, for the real Computer Science, Mathematics and Statistics courses; the catalog facts for those courses stay in grinnell_catalog.json.

courses.title: Introduction to Art History
courses.description: Surveys painting, sculpture and architecture from antiquity to the present, with attention to how images carry meaning. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.

courses.title: Art of the Ancient Mediterranean
courses.description: Examines the art and architecture of Egypt, Greece and Rome in their political and religious settings. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Medieval and Renaissance Art
courses.description: Traces European art from illuminated manuscripts to the workshops of fifteenth-century Italy and Flanders. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: European Art from Baroque to Impressionism
courses.description: Follows three centuries of European painting and sculpture, from court patronage to the independent exhibition. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Modern and Contemporary Art
courses.description: Considers the major movements of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries and the debates that shaped them. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Arts of East Asia
courses.description: Introduces the painting, ceramics and built environments of China, Korea and Japan. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Methods of Art History
courses.description: Introduces the questions art historians ask, from formal analysis and iconography to social history and critical theory. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Seminar: Art and Empire
courses.description: Investigates how empires have collected, displayed and produced art, and how artists have answered back. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Seminar: Museums and Collecting
courses.description: Studies the museum as an institution: how collections are formed, interpreted and contested. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Seminar: Image and Devotion
courses.description: Explores sacred images across several traditions and the practices of looking, touching and veneration around them. Enrollment is limited, and each student writes a substantial research paper developed over the semester.

courses.title: Seminar: Photography and Modernity
courses.description: Considers photography from its invention to the digital image as both an art form and a social technology. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Art History
courses.description: Majors design and complete an independent research project and present it to the department. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Beginning Chinese I
courses.description: Introduces spoken Mandarin and the writing system through daily practice in listening, speaking, reading and character writing. Daily homework, short quizzes and oral practice keep the pace steady throughout the term.

courses.title: Beginning Chinese II
courses.description: Continues the first-year sequence, extending vocabulary and grammar for everyday conversation and short written texts. Daily homework, short quizzes and oral practice keep the pace steady throughout the term.

courses.title: Intermediate Chinese I
courses.description: Builds fluency through longer dialogues, short essays and a growing stock of characters. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Intermediate Chinese II
courses.description: Completes the intermediate sequence with authentic readings, presentations and regular composition. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Chinese Cinema in Translation
courses.description: Surveys films from mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan and the histories they reflect; taught in English. Students complete weekly writing assignments and a final project.

courses.title: Modern China through Literature
courses.description: Reads fiction and essays from the late Qing to the present as a window on social change; taught in English. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Classical Chinese Thought in Translation
courses.description: Introduces Confucian, Daoist and Legalist texts and their long afterlives; taught in English. Students complete weekly writing assignments and a final project.

courses.title: Advanced Chinese: Media and Society
courses.description: Uses news, television and online writing to develop advanced reading and discussion skills. The course is conducted in the language, and students write and present a final paper.

courses.title: Advanced Chinese: Short Fiction
courses.description: Reads modern short stories in the original, with attention to style, register and translation. The course is conducted in the language, and students write and present a final paper.

courses.title: Readings in Classical Chinese
courses.description: Introduces the grammar of the classical language through short passages of philosophy, history and poetry. The course is conducted in the language, and students write and present a final paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Translation Workshop
courses.description: Students translate literary and documentary texts and study the choices translators make. The course is conducted in the language, and students write and present a final paper.

courses.title: Senior Project in Chinese
courses.description: Majors carry out a sustained research or translation project using Chinese-language sources. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Classical Mythology
courses.description: Reads the major myths of Greece and Rome in ancient sources and follows their retellings in later art and literature. Open to all students; the course emphasizes careful reading, discussion and analytical writing.

courses.title: The Greek World from Homer to Alexander
courses.description: Surveys Greek history and culture from the Bronze Age to the conquests of Alexander. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Rome: Republic and Empire
courses.description: Follows Rome from a city-state on the Tiber to a Mediterranean empire, using literary and material evidence. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Greek Archaeology and Art
courses.description: Studies the material culture of the Greek world from the Bronze Age to the Hellenistic kingdoms through excavated sites and objects. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once. Cross-listed as ARH-248.

courses.title: Greek Archaeology and Art
courses.description: Studies the material culture of the Greek world from the Bronze Age to the Hellenistic kingdoms through excavated sites and objects. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once. Cross-listed as CLS-248.

courses.title: Ancient Drama
courses.description: Reads Greek tragedy and comedy with attention to staging, festival context and modern performance. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Gender in Antiquity
courses.description: Examines how Greek and Roman societies imagined gender, family and the body. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Elementary Latin
courses.description: Introduces Latin grammar and vocabulary with the aim of reading continuous prose by the end of the term. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.

courses.title: Intermediate Latin: Prose and Poetry
courses.description: Reads selections from Cicero, Catullus and Vergil while reviewing grammar. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Elementary Greek
courses.description: Introduces the forms and syntax of classical Attic Greek through graded readings. Open to all students; the course emphasizes careful reading, discussion and analytical writing.

courses.title: Intermediate Greek: Homer
courses.description: Reads selections from the Iliad or the Odyssey and introduces epic dialect and meter. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Epic and Its Afterlives
courses.description: Studies ancient epic and its reception from late antiquity to contemporary fiction. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Law and Society in Rome
courses.description: Uses legal texts, speeches and inscriptions to study how Romans argued about property, family and status. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Athenian Democracy and Its Critics
courses.description: Examines the institutions of democratic Athens alongside the thinkers who attacked and defended them. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Classics
courses.description: Majors pursue an independent research project on a shared theme and present it publicly. Normally taken in the senior year; the course ends with a public presentation.

courses.title: Literary Analysis
courses.description: Introduces the close reading of poetry, fiction and drama and the craft of writing about literature. Class meetings are mostly discussion, and writing assignments move from brief responses to a longer paper.

courses.title: Introduction to Shakespeare
courses.description: Reads a selection of comedies, histories and tragedies with attention to language and performance. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.

courses.title: The Craft of Fiction
courses.description: A workshop in short fiction: students read published stories as writers and draft and revise their own. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: The Craft of Poetry
courses.description: A workshop in poetry that pairs the study of form and line with weekly writing. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: The Tradition of English Literature I
courses.description: Surveys literature in English from the medieval period through the seventeenth century. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: The Tradition of English Literature II
courses.description: Surveys British literature from the Restoration to the early twentieth century. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: American Literary Traditions
courses.description: Reads American writing from the colonial period to the present and asks what has counted as an American tradition. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term. Cross-listed as AMS-227.

courses.title: American Literary Traditions
courses.description: Reads American writing from the colonial period to the present and asks what has counted as an American tradition. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term. Cross-listed as ENG-227.

courses.title: Global Anglophone Literature
courses.description: Studies fiction and poetry in English from Africa, South Asia and the Caribbean. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Literature and the Environment
courses.description: Considers how writers have imagined land, climate and nonhuman life, from pastoral to climate fiction. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Introduction to Literary Theory
courses.description: Introduces the major schools of literary and cultural theory and puts them to work on shared texts. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Seminar: Studies in the Novel
courses.description: Follows the novel as a form across two centuries, with one long novel read slowly at the center of the term. Enrollment is limited, and each student writes a substantial research paper developed over the semester.

courses.title: Seminar: Poetry and Poetics
courses.description: Studies a small group of poets in depth alongside their essays, letters and critics. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Seminar: Race and American Narrative
courses.description: Examines how American fiction and memoir have constructed and contested ideas of race. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Writing Seminar: Fiction
courses.description: An advanced workshop in which each student completes a portfolio of revised stories. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in English
courses.description: Majors write a substantial critical or creative project and workshop it with their peers. Required of all majors and normally taken in the final year.

courses.title: Introductory French I
courses.description: Develops basic speaking, listening, reading and writing skills in French through daily practice. Class meets four days a week and is conducted in the language as far as possible.

courses.title: Introductory French II
courses.description: Continues the introductory sequence and introduces short texts from across the French-speaking world. Class meets four days a week and is conducted in the language as far as possible.

courses.title: Intermediate French I
courses.description: Reviews and extends grammar while building confidence in conversation and composition. Students complete weekly writing assignments and a final project.

courses.title: Intermediate French II
courses.description: Prepares students for advanced work through film, short fiction and sustained writing in French. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Paris and the Francophone City
courses.description: Studies Paris, Dakar and Montreal as sites of migration, protest and artistic invention; taught in English. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: Francophone Cinema
courses.description: Surveys film from France, West Africa and Quebec; taught in English. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: French Civilization: Revolution to Republic
courses.description: Follows French political and cultural history from 1789 to the present through documents, images and film. The course is conducted in the language, and students write and present a final paper.

courses.title: Contemporary Francophone Cultures
courses.description: Examines language, identity and politics in the French-speaking Caribbean, Maghreb and sub-Saharan Africa. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Introduction to French Literature
courses.description: Introduces literary analysis in French through poetry, theater and prose from several centuries. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Seminar: Caribbean and African Voices in French
courses.description: Reads novels and essays by Francophone writers on colonialism, memory and language. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Advanced Composition and Translation
courses.description: Refines written French through stylistic exercises and translation in both directions. The course is conducted in the language, and students write and present a final paper.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in French
courses.description: Majors complete and present a research project written in French. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Introductory German I
courses.description: Introduces German for everyday communication, with equal weight on speaking, listening, reading and writing. Class meets four days a week and is conducted in the language as far as possible.

courses.title: Introductory German II
courses.description: Continues the introductory sequence with short readings on contemporary life in German-speaking countries. Small-group practice sessions with a language assistant supplement regular class meetings.

courses.title: Intermediate German I
courses.description: Strengthens grammar and vocabulary through film, journalism and discussion. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: Intermediate German II
courses.description: Moves toward advanced work with longer texts and regular essays in German. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: German Film
courses.description: Surveys German cinema from Expressionism to the present; taught in English. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Berlin: Capital of the Twentieth Century
courses.description: Uses one city to study empire, dictatorship, division and reunification; taught in English. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Contemporary Issues in German
courses.description: Builds advanced speaking and writing skills around current debates in the German-language press. Students lead discussion and complete a research paper drawing on original-language sources.

courses.title: Readings in German Literature
courses.description: Introduces literary analysis in German through short prose, drama and poetry. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Migration and Identity in German-Speaking Europe
courses.description: Studies literature, film and policy debates on migration and belonging. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Seminar: Weimar Culture
courses.description: Examines the art, film and political writing of the Weimar Republic. Students lead discussion and complete a research paper drawing on original-language sources.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in German Studies
courses.description: Majors research and write a capstone essay in German and present it to the department. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Music
courses.description: Teaches notation, scales, intervals and basic keyboard skills to students with little or no formal training. Class combines practical work with listening, viewing and short written reflections.

courses.title: Performance Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearses and performs in one of the department's ensembles; may be repeated for credit. No previous training is required; attendance at several campus performances is expected.

courses.title: Harmony and Musicianship I
courses.description: Introduces tonal harmony, voice leading and ear training through writing, singing and keyboard work. Regular practice outside class is expected, along with short written assignments.

courses.title: Music, Culture, Context
courses.description: Asks how music works in social life, drawing on examples from many traditions and periods. No previous training is required; attendance at several campus performances is expected.

courses.title: Harmony and Musicianship II
courses.description: Continues the study of harmony into chromaticism and larger forms, with continued aural training. Class time is divided between studio work and discussion.

courses.title: Introduction to Composition
courses.description: Students write short pieces for small ensembles and hear them read by performers. Assignments include weekly exercises, a midterm project and a final showing or paper.

courses.title: Electronic Music
courses.description: Covers recording, synthesis and sequencing in the studio, alongside the history of electronic sound. Class time is divided between studio work and discussion.

courses.title: Western Music to 1750
courses.description: Surveys European art music from chant to the late Baroque in its cultural setting. Students complete practical projects alongside readings and a short research paper.

courses.title: Western Music since 1750
courses.description: Follows art music from the Classical style through the twentieth century and beyond. Students complete practical projects alongside readings and a short research paper.

courses.title: Regional Studies in World Music
courses.description: Studies the music of one region in depth, combining listening, reading and hands-on performance. Students complete practical projects alongside readings and a short research paper.

courses.title: Jazz Traditions
courses.description: Traces jazz from its roots to the present through recordings, biography and social history. Students complete practical projects alongside readings and a short research paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Advanced Analysis
courses.description: Applies several analytical methods to works from the eighteenth century to the present. Students present work in progress throughout the term and complete a final project.

courses.title: Seminar: Music and Politics
courses.description: Examines censorship, patronage, protest and propaganda in music across several periods. Students present work in progress throughout the term and complete a final project.

courses.title: Seminar: Opera and Society
courses.description: Studies a handful of operas closely as drama, music and social event. Each student leads a session and completes a substantial final paper or performance.

courses.title: Senior Project in Music
courses.description: Majors prepare a recital, composition portfolio or research paper with a faculty mentor. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: Introduces central questions about knowledge, reality, freedom and the good life through classic and recent texts. Class meetings are mostly discussion, and writing assignments move from brief responses to a longer paper.

courses.title: Symbolic Logic
courses.description: Teaches the formal languages of sentential and predicate logic and their use in evaluating arguments. Class meetings are mostly discussion, and writing assignments move from brief responses to a longer paper.

courses.title: Ancient Greek Philosophy
courses.description: Reads the Presocratics, Plato and Aristotle on nature, knowledge and virtue. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Early Modern Philosophy
courses.description: Follows debates about mind, matter and knowledge from Descartes to Hume. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Ethical Theory
courses.description: Compares consequentialist, deontological and virtue-based accounts of right action. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Philosophy of Mind
courses.description: Examines consciousness, mental representation and the relation between mind and brain. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Philosophy of Science
courses.description: Asks what distinguishes scientific explanation, how theories are confirmed and how they change. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Political Theory
courses.description: Reads major works of political thought on justice, liberty, authority and equality. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once. Cross-listed as POL-263.

courses.title: Political Theory
courses.description: Reads major works of political thought on justice, liberty, authority and equality. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once. Cross-listed as PHI-263.

courses.title: Philosophy of Race and Gender
courses.description: Examines what race and gender are, and what follows for questions of justice and identity. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Seminar: Kant
courses.description: A close reading of the Critique of Pure Reason and its reception. Enrollment is limited, and each student writes a substantial research paper developed over the semester.

courses.title: Seminar: Metaethics
courses.description: Investigates whether moral claims can be true, known or motivating. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Seminar: Minds and Machines
courses.description: Considers whether machines can think, understand or be held responsible. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Contemporary Epistemology
courses.description: Studies recent work on knowledge, justification, testimony and disagreement. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Philosophy
courses.description: Majors write and defend a substantial essay on a topic of their choosing. Normally taken in the senior year; the course ends with a public presentation.

courses.title: Introduction to the Study of Religion
courses.description: Asks what religion is and how scholars study it, using case studies from several traditions. Class meetings are mostly discussion, and writing assignments move from brief responses to a longer paper.

courses.title: The Hebrew Bible
courses.description: Reads the Hebrew Bible as literature and as a record of ancient Israel, with attention to modern scholarship. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Christian Traditions
courses.description: Surveys the history, texts and practices of Christianity from its origins to the present. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Islam: Texts and Communities
courses.description: Introduces the Qur'an, law, mysticism and the diversity of Muslim life across regions. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Buddhist Traditions
courses.description: Follows Buddhist thought and practice from early India across Asia and into the modern West. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Religions of South Asia
courses.description: Studies Hindu, Jain, Sikh and Muslim traditions of the subcontinent and their interactions. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Religion in the United States
courses.description: Examines religious pluralism, revival and conflict in American public life. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Religion, Ethics and Environment
courses.description: Considers how religious communities understand and respond to environmental change. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Theory and Method in the Study of Religion
courses.description: Reads the theorists who shaped the field and tests their approaches against particular cases. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Seminar: Mysticism
courses.description: Compares accounts of mystical experience and asks how they can be interpreted. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Seminar: Religion and Law
courses.description: Studies how courts and states define religion, and how religious traditions understand law. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Ritual and Performance
courses.description: Uses ethnography and theory to study ritual as embodied action. Enrollment is limited, and each student writes a substantial research paper developed over the semester.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Religious Studies
courses.description: Majors develop an independent research project and present it at a department colloquium. Normally taken in the senior year; the course ends with a public presentation.

courses.title: Beginning Russian I
courses.description: Introduces the Cyrillic alphabet, basic grammar and everyday conversation. Class meets four days a week and is conducted in the language as far as possible.

courses.title: Beginning Russian II
courses.description: Continues the first-year sequence, completing the case system and introducing short readings. Daily homework, short quizzes and oral practice keep the pace steady throughout the term.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian I
courses.description: Reviews grammar and expands vocabulary through film clips, songs and short stories. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian II
courses.description: Develops reading and discussion skills with unadapted texts and regular writing. Students complete weekly writing assignments and a final project.

courses.title: The Russian Short Story
courses.description: Reads short fiction from Pushkin to the present; taught in English. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Russian and Soviet Film
courses.description: Surveys cinema from the montage school to contemporary directors; taught in English. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: Advanced Russian: Reading the Press
courses.description: Uses newspapers, broadcasts and online media to build advanced comprehension. Students lead discussion and complete a research paper drawing on original-language sources.

courses.title: Advanced Russian: Conversation and Composition
courses.description: Focuses on spoken fluency and stylistically varied writing. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Readings in Russian Poetry
courses.description: Introduces Russian verse from the Golden Age to the twentieth century in the original. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Seminar: Tolstoy and Dostoevsky
courses.description: Reads major works by the two novelists, partly in Russian, with attention to their philosophical stakes. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Russian
courses.description: Majors complete a research project that draws on Russian-language sources. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Introductory Spanish I
courses.description: Develops basic communication skills in Spanish through daily speaking, listening, reading and writing. Small-group practice sessions with a language assistant supplement regular class meetings.

courses.title: Introductory Spanish II
courses.description: Continues the introductory sequence with more complex structures and short cultural readings. Small-group practice sessions with a language assistant supplement regular class meetings.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I
courses.description: Reviews grammar and builds vocabulary through film, news and conversation. Readings, screenings and discussion are supported by short papers.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II
courses.description: Prepares students for advanced courses with short literary texts and regular essays. Students complete weekly writing assignments and a final project.

courses.title: Latinx Cultures in the United States
courses.description: Studies literature, music and film by Latinx artists and the communities they come from; taught in English. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: Spain Today
courses.description: Examines politics, regional identity and popular culture in contemporary Spain; taught in English. Regular written work and oral presentations are required.

courses.title: Constructing Identities in Latin America
courses.description: Reads essays, fiction and film on nation, race and belonging from independence to the present. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Modern Spanish Narrative
courses.description: Follows the Spanish novel and short story from realism through the post-Franco period. The course is conducted in the language, and students write and present a final paper.

courses.title: Cultures of Spain
courses.description: Surveys the history, art and languages of the Iberian Peninsula. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: The Art of Language
courses.description: An advanced study of Spanish grammar and style through close analysis and writing. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Seminar: Borders and Migration
courses.description: Studies narratives of crossing, exile and return in the Spanish-speaking world. Discussion and all written work are in the language.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Spanish
courses.description: Majors research, write and present a capstone essay in Spanish. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Introduction to the Studio
courses.description: Introduces the materials, methods and vocabulary of studio practice across two and three dimensions. No experience is required; students complete a series of projects and take part in critiques.

courses.title: Drawing
courses.description: Develops observational drawing through line, value and composition in a range of media. No experience is required; students complete a series of projects and take part in critiques.

courses.title: Print Media
courses.description: Covers relief, intaglio and screen printing and the idea of the multiple. Students complete four or five projects and present them in critique.

courses.title: Painting
courses.description: Introduces oil and acrylic painting, color mixing and the construction of pictorial space. Studio work is supported by readings, artist talks and a sketchbook.

courses.title: Ceramics
courses.description: Teaches hand-building, wheel throwing and glazing as approaches to functional and sculptural form. Studio work is supported by readings, artist talks and a sketchbook.

courses.title: Sculpture
courses.description: Explores wood, metal and found materials and the relation of objects to space. Students complete four or five projects and present them in critique.

courses.title: Digital Media
courses.description: Uses image editing, video and code as tools for making art. Students complete four or five projects and present them in critique.

courses.title: Photography
courses.description: Covers camera technique, lighting and editing alongside the history of the photographic image. Students complete four or five projects and present them in critique.

courses.title: Advanced Studio: Site and Installation
courses.description: Students make work for particular places and audiences, on and off campus. The course ends with a public installation of student work.

courses.title: Advanced Studio: Contemporary Practices
courses.description: Students develop a self-directed body of work in conversation with current art. Individual studio visits, readings and critiques structure the semester.

courses.title: Advanced Studio: Image and Sequence
courses.description: Explores series, books and time-based work across print, photography and video. Students work independently toward a coherent body of work, with weekly critiques.

courses.title: Senior Exhibition Seminar
courses.description: Majors produce and install a body of work for the senior exhibition and write an artist statement. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Contemporary Dance Technique
courses.description: Builds strength, alignment and movement vocabulary in contemporary dance. Class combines practical work with listening, viewing and short written reflections.

courses.title: Introduction to Performance Studies
courses.description: Introduces theatre, dance and everyday performance as objects of study and as ways of knowing. No previous training is required; attendance at several campus performances is expected.

courses.title: Theatrical Design and Technology
courses.description: Introduces scenic, lighting and costume design and the crafts that realize them. Regular practice outside class is expected, along with short written assignments.

courses.title: Introduction to Acting
courses.description: Develops the actor's voice, body and imagination through exercises, scenes and monologues. Class combines practical work with listening, viewing and short written reflections.

courses.title: World Theatre History
courses.description: Surveys performance traditions from several continents and the societies that produced them. Students complete practical projects alongside readings and a short research paper.

courses.title: Directing
courses.description: Covers script analysis, staging and work with actors, ending in a directed scene. Class time is divided between studio work and discussion.

courses.title: Choreography and Composition
courses.description: Students create short dances while studying structure, space and time. Assignments include weekly exercises, a midterm project and a final showing or paper.

courses.title: Playwriting
courses.description: A workshop in writing for the stage, from short scenes to a one-act play. Assignments include weekly exercises, a midterm project and a final showing or paper.

courses.title: Scenic and Lighting Design
courses.description: Takes design projects from concept through drafting, models and light plots. Assignments include weekly exercises, a midterm project and a final showing or paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Performance Theory
courses.description: Reads theories of performance, spectatorship and embodiment alongside live and recorded work. Each student leads a session and completes a substantial final paper or performance.

courses.title: Studio: Devised Performance
courses.description: An ensemble creates an original piece from research, improvisation and collaborative writing. The course combines close study with a culminating public presentation.

courses.title: Seminar: Dance, Body and Culture
courses.description: Studies dance as social practice across cultures and periods. The course combines close study with a culminating public presentation.

courses.title: Senior Capstone in Theatre and Dance
courses.description: Majors complete a performance, design or research project and reflect on it in writing. Required of all majors and normally taken in the final year.

courses.title: Molecules of Life
courses.description: Introduces the chemistry of proteins, nucleic acids, lipids and sugars for students curious about the molecular basis of biology. A weekly three-hour laboratory introduces experimental design and data analysis.

courses.title: Introduction to Biological Chemistry
courses.description: Covers the structure and function of biological macromolecules, enzyme catalysis and the central pathways of metabolism. Class meetings are paired with a weekly three-hour laboratory.

courses.title: Biophysical Chemistry
courses.description: Applies thermodynamics, kinetics and spectroscopy to biological molecules. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Protein Structure and Function
courses.description: Examines how proteins fold, bind and catalyze, using structures from the current literature. Students read the primary literature and complete an extended laboratory or field project.

courses.title: Nucleic Acids and Gene Regulation
courses.description: Studies the chemistry of DNA and RNA and the molecular machinery that controls gene expression. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Enzyme Kinetics and Mechanism
courses.description: Works through how enzymes achieve their rates and specificity, with quantitative analysis of kinetic data. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Metabolism and Disease
courses.description: Follows metabolic pathways and their regulation, and what goes wrong in diabetes, cancer and inherited disorders. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Laboratory Methods in Biochemistry
courses.description: A project-based laboratory in protein purification, assays and molecular cloning. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Chemical Biology
courses.description: Uses synthetic molecules as probes of living systems, from drug design to imaging. Students read the primary literature and complete an extended laboratory or field project.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Biological Chemistry
courses.description: Majors read, present and critique current research, and write a review article. Normally taken in the senior year; the course ends with a public presentation.

courses.title: Introduction to Biological Inquiry
courses.description: Students learn how biologists ask and answer questions by designing and carrying out their own investigations. Three class meetings and one laboratory each week.

courses.title: Animal Behavior
courses.description: Examines how and why animals behave as they do, from mechanisms to evolutionary function. Problem sets and laboratory work carry equal weight.

courses.title: Molecules, Cells and Organisms
courses.description: Covers cell structure, metabolism, genetics and the molecular basis of physiology. Includes a weekly laboratory, with formal lab reports.

courses.title: Organisms, Evolution and Ecology
courses.description: Studies the diversity of life, the processes of evolution and the interactions of organisms with their environments. Problem sets and laboratory work carry equal weight.

courses.title: Plant Diversity and Evolution
courses.description: Surveys the major plant lineages and the evidence for their relationships, with field and herbarium work. Students read the primary literature and complete an extended laboratory or field project.

courses.title: Microbiology
courses.description: Introduces bacteria, archaea and viruses: their physiology, genetics and roles in health and ecosystems. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Animal Physiology
courses.description: Compares how animals solve problems of respiration, circulation, water balance and movement. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Advanced Genetics
courses.description: Examines gene structure, inheritance and genomics using classical and molecular approaches. Students read the primary literature and complete an extended laboratory or field project.

courses.title: Neurobiology
courses.description: Covers the cellular and molecular basis of nervous system function, from ion channels to circuits. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Conservation Biology
courses.description: Applies population biology and ecology to the protection of species and habitats. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Ecology
courses.description: Studies populations, communities and ecosystems, with field projects at the college's prairie research area. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Mechanisms of Evolution
courses.description: Examines selection, drift and speciation using population genetics and case studies. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Senior Research Seminar in Biology
courses.description: Majors present their own or published research and write a research proposal. Required of all majors and normally taken in the final year.

courses.title: General Chemistry
courses.description: Introduces atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, equilibrium and thermodynamics. Lecture, problem solving and a weekly laboratory are closely integrated.

courses.title: Inorganic and Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Covers periodic trends, coordination chemistry and the quantitative analysis of solutions. Class meetings are paired with a weekly three-hour laboratory.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: Introduces the structure, reactivity and synthesis of carbon compounds. Problem sets and laboratory work carry equal weight.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: Continues organic chemistry with carbonyl compounds, aromatic systems and multi-step synthesis. Problem sets and laboratory work carry equal weight.

courses.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Examines reaction mechanisms, stereochemistry and modern synthetic methods. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Instrumental Analysis
courses.description: Covers the theory and practice of spectroscopy, chromatography and electrochemical methods. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Environmental Chemistry
courses.description: Applies chemical principles to air, water and soil, with field sampling and analysis. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Studies bonding, symmetry and reactivity in transition-metal and main-group compounds. Students read the primary literature and complete an extended laboratory or field project.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry I
courses.description: Develops thermodynamics and chemical kinetics from first principles. Students read the primary literature and complete an extended laboratory or field project.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry II
courses.description: Introduces quantum mechanics and its application to atomic and molecular spectroscopy. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Materials Chemistry
courses.description: Examines polymers, semiconductors and nanomaterials and how structure determines their properties. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Chemistry
courses.description: Majors present current research from the literature and write a critical review. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: The Universe and Its Structure
courses.description: A descriptive introduction to astronomy and cosmology for students in any field. Three class meetings and one laboratory each week.

courses.title: General Physics I
courses.description: Introduces mechanics: motion, forces, energy, momentum and rotation. Three class meetings and one laboratory each week.

courses.title: General Physics II
courses.description: Continues with electricity, magnetism, circuits and optics. Lecture, problem solving and a weekly laboratory are closely integrated.

courses.title: Electronics
courses.description: Covers analog and digital circuits through design projects at the bench. Class meetings are paired with a weekly three-hour laboratory.

courses.title: Modern Physics
courses.description: Introduces special relativity, quantum ideas and the structure of atoms and nuclei. Problem sets and laboratory work carry equal weight.

courses.title: Classical Mechanics
courses.description: Develops Newtonian and Lagrangian mechanics, oscillations and central-force motion. Class meetings are paired with a weekly three-hour laboratory.

courses.title: Computational Physics
courses.description: Uses numerical methods and simulation to solve problems that resist pen-and-paper solutions. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
courses.description: Develops electrostatics, magnetostatics and Maxwell's equations using vector calculus. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Optics and Waves
courses.description: Studies interference, diffraction, polarization and lasers, with laboratory projects. Students read the primary literature and complete an extended laboratory or field project.

courses.title: Astrophysics
courses.description: Applies physics to stars, galaxies and cosmology. Includes a project-based laboratory and a final written report in journal format.

courses.title: Solid State Physics
courses.description: Examines crystal structure, electrons in solids and the physics of semiconductors. Class discussion centers on recent papers, and the laboratory supports an independent project.

courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Develops the formal theory of quantum mechanics and applies it to simple systems. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Students carry out and report on a series of open-ended experiments in modern physics. Required of all majors and normally taken in the final year.

courses.title: Introduction to Psychology
courses.description: Surveys the scientific study of behavior and mind, from the brain to social life. Lectures are paired with problem sets, and two exams and a final are given.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Examines how other people shape attitudes, judgment and behavior. The course combines lecture with hands-on work and a short empirical paper.

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: Teaches experimental and correlational design, measurement and the reporting of results. The course combines lecture with hands-on work and a short empirical paper.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Follows cognitive, social and emotional change from infancy through adolescence. Students analyze data with statistical software and write up their findings.

courses.title: Learning and Behavior
courses.description: Studies conditioning, reinforcement and their applications. Students analyze data with statistical software and write up their findings.

courses.title: Brain and Behavior
courses.description: Introduces the neural basis of perception, motivation, memory and emotion. Problem sets, a data project and exams are required.

courses.title: Psychopathology
courses.description: Examines the description, causes and treatment of psychological disorders. Problem sets, a data project and exams are required.

courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Covers attention, memory, language and decision making. Students analyze data with statistical software and write up their findings.

courses.title: Advanced Social Psychology
courses.description: Students design and run an original study on a current question in social psychology. The course ends with a research paper and presentation.

courses.title: Advanced Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Examines current research on development, with an observational research project. Students read current research and complete an original empirical project.

courses.title: Advanced Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description: Reads primary literature on the neural mechanisms of behavior and practices laboratory techniques. Students read current research and complete an original empirical project.

courses.title: Seminar in Clinical Science
courses.description: Evaluates the evidence for psychological treatments and how it is produced. Enrollment is limited; students present papers from the literature and write a research report.

courses.title: Advanced Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Students replicate and extend a published experiment on memory or attention. The course ends with a research paper and presentation.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Psychology
courses.description: Majors integrate their coursework around a contested question and write a review paper. Normally taken in the senior year; the course ends with a public presentation.

courses.title: Anthropological Inquiry
courses.description: Introduces the four fields of anthropology and the ways anthropologists study human variation. Lectures and discussion introduce key concepts, and students write several short papers.

courses.title: Human Evolution
courses.description: Examines the fossil, genetic and archaeological evidence for the origins of our species. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Illness, Healing and Culture
courses.description: Studies how societies understand sickness and organize care. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Archaeology of North America
courses.description: Surveys the continent's deep history from the first peoples to the colonial era. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Language and Culture
courses.description: Explores how language shapes identity, power and everyday interaction. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Environmental Anthropology
courses.description: Considers how communities live with, know and contest their environments. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Anthropology of Food
courses.description: Uses food to study exchange, ritual, labor and inequality. Readings combine classic studies with recent research, and students write a final paper.

courses.title: Theories of Culture
courses.description: Traces the history of anthropological thought through its central debates. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Ethnographic Research Methods
courses.description: Students practice observation, interviewing and field notes in a local research project. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Seminar: Migration and Belonging
courses.description: Reads ethnographies of movement, borders and citizenship. Students lead discussion on the readings and present a seminar paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Bioarchaeology
courses.description: Studies what human remains reveal about health, labor and identity in the past. Enrollment is limited, and each student completes an original research paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Anthropology of the State
courses.description: Examines bureaucracy, law and policing as lived experience. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Seminar: Experimental Ethnography
courses.description: Explores film, sound and creative writing as forms of anthropological knowledge. Students lead discussion on the readings and present a seminar paper.

courses.title: Senior Thesis Seminar in Anthropology
courses.description: Majors write a thesis based on original field, laboratory or archival research. Open to senior majors, who meet weekly to share work in progress.

courses.title: Introduction to Economics
courses.description: Introduces how markets work, when they fail, and how the economy as a whole grows and fluctuates. Students work with data and simple models from the first week.

courses.title: Current Economic Issues
courses.description: Applies introductory tools to debates on trade, inequality, health care and climate policy. The course combines lecture with hands-on work and a short empirical paper.

courses.title: Labor Economics
courses.description: Studies wages, employment, unions and discrimination in the labor market. The course combines lecture with hands-on work and a short empirical paper.

courses.title: Environmental Economics
courses.description: Examines pollution, natural resources and the design of environmental policy. Problem sets, a data project and exams are required.

courses.title: Economic Development
courses.description: Asks why some countries are rich and others poor, and what policies change that. The course combines lecture with hands-on work and a short empirical paper.

courses.title: Money and Banking
courses.description: Covers financial institutions, central banking and monetary policy. The course combines lecture with hands-on work and a short empirical paper.

courses.title: Microeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Develops the theory of consumers, firms and markets using calculus. Problem sets, a data project and exams are required.

courses.title: Macroeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Builds models of growth, unemployment and inflation and uses them to evaluate policy. Problem sets, a data project and exams are required.

courses.title: Econometrics
courses.description: Teaches regression analysis and causal inference with economic data. Problem sets, a data project and exams are required.

courses.title: Seminar in Industrial Organization
courses.description: Studies competition, market power and antitrust. Enrollment is limited; students present papers from the literature and write a research report.

courses.title: Seminar in Applied Game Theory
courses.description: Uses strategic models to analyze bargaining, auctions and cooperation. Enrollment is limited; students present papers from the literature and write a research report.

courses.title: Seminar in International Trade
courses.description: Examines why countries trade, who gains and how trade policy is made. Students read current research and complete an original empirical project.

courses.title: Seminar in Public Finance
courses.description: Analyzes taxation, public spending and social insurance, with an empirical research paper. Enrollment is limited; students present papers from the literature and write a research report.

courses.title: Historical Methods
courses.description: Introduces how historians find, read and argue from evidence, organized around one topic chosen by the instructor. No background is assumed; assignments include reading responses, two exams and a short paper.

courses.title: Colonial Latin America
courses.description: Follows the Americas from the eve of conquest to the wars of independence. Students write two essays and complete a small research project. Cross-listed as LAS-201.

courses.title: Colonial Latin America
courses.description: Follows the Americas from the eve of conquest to the wars of independence. Students write two essays and complete a small research project. Cross-listed as HIS-201.

courses.title: The United States to 1877
courses.description: Surveys North America from colonization through Reconstruction. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: The United States since 1877
courses.description: Follows the United States from the Gilded Age to the present. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Modern Europe, 1789 to the Present
courses.description: Traces revolution, industrialization, war and integration in European history. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Britain and Empire
courses.description: Studies the rise and unraveling of the British Empire and its effects at home and abroad. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: East Asia since 1600
courses.description: Compares the modern histories of China, Japan and Korea. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Africa since 1800
courses.description: Examines the slave trades, colonial rule, independence and the postcolonial state. Readings combine classic studies with recent research, and students write a final paper.

courses.title: The Modern Middle East
courses.description: Follows the region from the late Ottoman period to the present. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Seminar: The American West
courses.description: Reads recent scholarship on land, migration and myth in the West. Students lead discussion on the readings and present a seminar paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Revolution and Memory in Europe
courses.description: Studies how revolutions have been remembered, commemorated and argued over. Enrollment is limited, and each student completes an original research paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Decolonization
courses.description: Compares the end of empire in Asia, Africa and the Caribbean. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Seminar: Oral History and Public Memory
courses.description: Students conduct interviews and produce a public history project. Students lead discussion on the readings and present a seminar paper.

courses.title: Introduction to Political Science
courses.description: Introduces the study of power, institutions and political behavior in the United States and abroad. Students practice reading evidence critically and writing clear, well-supported arguments.

courses.title: American Political Institutions
courses.description: Examines Congress, the presidency and the bureaucracy and how they interact. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Constitutional Law and Politics
courses.description: Reads landmark Supreme Court decisions on federal power and individual rights. Readings combine classic studies with recent research, and students write a final paper.

courses.title: Empirical Political Analysis
courses.description: Teaches research design and the use of quantitative and qualitative evidence in political science. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Politics of International Relations
courses.description: Introduces theories of war, cooperation and international order. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: International Political Economy
courses.description: Studies the politics of trade, finance and development. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Comparative Democracies
courses.description: Compares electoral systems, parties and welfare states across established democracies. Readings combine classic studies with recent research, and students write a final paper.

courses.title: Politics of Development
courses.description: Examines state building, inequality and reform in the Global South. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Seminar: Courts and Rights
courses.description: Asks when courts protect rights and when they do not. Enrollment is limited, and each student completes an original research paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Parties and Polarization
courses.description: Studies the causes and consequences of partisan division. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Seminar: United States Foreign Policy
courses.description: Analyzes how foreign policy is made and debated, through historical cases. Enrollment is limited, and each student completes an original research paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Democratic Backsliding
courses.description: Compares how democracies erode and how they recover. Enrollment is limited, and each student completes an original research paper.

courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.description: Introduces the sociological study of groups, institutions and inequality. Lectures and discussion introduce key concepts, and students write several short papers.

courses.title: Sociology of Global Development
courses.description: Examines theories of development and the institutions that shape global inequality. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Social Movements
courses.description: Studies why movements emerge, how they organize and when they succeed. Readings combine classic studies with recent research, and students write a final paper.

courses.title: Self and Society
courses.description: Introduces social psychology from a sociological point of view: identity, interaction and emotion. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Sociology of the Family
courses.description: Examines how families are formed, how they vary and how policy shapes them. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Sociology of Health and Illness
courses.description: Studies the social causes of illness and the organization of medical care. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Gender and Society
courses.description: Examines gender as a social structure in work, family, schooling and the state. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam. Cross-listed as GWS-270.

courses.title: Gender and Society
courses.description: Examines gender as a social structure in work, family, schooling and the state. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam. Cross-listed as SOC-270.

courses.title: Race and Ethnicity in America
courses.description: Analyzes how racial categories are made and how they organize opportunity. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
courses.description: Reads the major theoretical traditions and applies them to current problems. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Methods of Empirical Investigation
courses.description: Teaches survey, interview and observational research, ending in a research proposal. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Seminar: Inequality and Education
courses.description: Examines how schools reproduce and disrupt inequality. Students lead discussion on the readings and present a seminar paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Organizations and Work
courses.description: Studies workplaces, professions and the changing employment relationship. Students lead discussion on the readings and present a seminar paper.

courses.title: Seminar: Urban Sociology
courses.description: Students study segregation, housing and neighborhood change with a local data project. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Seminar: Culture and Consumption
courses.description: Examines taste, markets and identity through original qualitative research. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Introduction to American Studies
courses.description: Introduces the interdisciplinary study of the United States through texts, images, music and places. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.

courses.title: Popular Culture in the United States
courses.description: Studies film, television, sport and advertising as evidence of social change. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Race, Place and Memory
courses.description: Examines monuments, museums and neighborhoods as sites where the past is argued over. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: The American Landscape
courses.description: Considers how prairies, suburbs and wilderness have been imagined and remade. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Immigration and Belonging
courses.description: Follows debates over who counts as American, from the nineteenth century to the present. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Methods in American Studies
courses.description: Practices archival research, visual analysis and oral history on shared case studies. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Seminar: The Midwest in the American Imagination
courses.description: Reads fiction, journalism and history about the region and tests them against local archives. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Music and Social Movements
courses.description: Studies the songs and performers tied to labor, civil rights and antiwar organizing. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Seminar: The Public Humanities
courses.description: Students design an exhibit, podcast or digital project with a community partner. Enrollment is limited, and each student writes a substantial research paper developed over the semester.

courses.title: Senior Project in American Studies
courses.description: Majors complete an interdisciplinary research or public project and present it. Required of all majors and normally taken in the final year.

courses.title: Introduction to Gender, Women's and Sexuality Studies
courses.description: Introduces gender and sexuality as categories of analysis and as lived experience. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.

courses.title: Foundations of LGBTQ Studies
courses.description: Surveys the history, politics and scholarship of LGBTQ communities. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Bodies, Health and Justice
courses.description: Examines reproductive politics, disability and access to care. Students write several analytical essays and lead discussion at least once.

courses.title: Feminist and Queer Media
courses.description: Studies film, television and online culture made by and about women and queer people. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Feminist and Queer Theory
courses.description: Reads the major theoretical texts of the field and the debates among them. Lecture and discussion alternate, and students complete a research-based paper by the end of the term.

courses.title: Transnational Feminisms
courses.description: Compares feminist movements across borders and the tensions among them. Assignments include response papers, a class presentation and a final essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Critical Race Feminisms
courses.description: Studies Black, Indigenous, Latina and Asian American feminist thought. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Seminar: Sexuality, Law and the State
courses.description: Examines how law regulates intimacy, family and identity. The course is reading-intensive and ends with an independent research essay.

courses.title: Seminar: Gender and Technology
courses.description: Asks how technologies from the contraceptive pill to the algorithm shape gender. Students take turns leading discussion and finish with a seminar paper presented to the class.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Gender, Women's and Sexuality Studies
courses.description: Majors complete a research or community-based project and present it. Required of all majors and normally taken in the final year.

courses.title: Introduction to Latin American Studies
courses.description: Introduces the region's histories, cultures and politics from several disciplines. Students practice reading evidence critically and writing clear, well-supported arguments.

courses.title: Modern Latin America
courses.description: Follows revolution, dictatorship and democratization from independence to the present. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Indigenous Peoples and the State
courses.description: Examines Indigenous movements, rights and autonomy in the Andes and Mesoamerica. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Caribbean Worlds
courses.description: Studies slavery, migration and cultural exchange across the islands and their diasporas. Readings combine classic studies with recent research, and students write a final paper.

courses.title: Cities of Latin America
courses.description: Uses Mexico City, Bogota and Sao Paulo to study urban growth, informality and culture. Readings combine classic studies with recent research, and students write a final paper.

courses.title: Political Economy of Latin America
courses.description: Analyzes commodity booms, debt and social policy. Assignments include discussion leadership, short papers and a final exam.

courses.title: Research Methods in Area Studies
courses.description: Introduces archival, ethnographic and quantitative approaches to studying a region. Students write two essays and complete a small research project.

courses.title: Seminar: Memory and Human Rights
courses.description: Studies truth commissions, trials and memorials after state violence. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Seminar: Borderlands
courses.description: Examines the border between the United States and Mexico as a region with its own history. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Seminar: Environment and Extraction
courses.description: Follows conflicts over mining, oil and forests and the communities involved. The seminar is organized around student research, developed in stages over the term.

courses.title: Senior Project in Latin American Studies
courses.description: Majors complete an interdisciplinary research project, normally using sources in Spanish or Portuguese. Normally taken in the senior year; the course ends with a public presentation.

courses.title: First-Year Tutorial
courses.description: A small writing-intensive seminar on a topic chosen by the instructor, who also serves as the student's first adviser. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.

courses.title: First-Year Experience
courses.description: Weekly sessions on navigating college life, academic planning and campus resources. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.
courses.note: The catalog policies name FYE-100 (S/D/F, typically the second semester, not repeatable) but give no course page; the 1 credit and the offering terms here are placeholders.

courses.title: Educational Principles
courses.description: Introduces the history, philosophy and politics of schooling in the United States. Class meetings are mostly discussion, and writing assignments move from brief responses to a longer paper.

courses.title: Introduction to Film Studies
courses.description: Teaches the vocabulary of film form and the major approaches to film history and criticism. No previous coursework in the field is assumed, and frequent short essays build the habits of close reading and argument.

courses.title: Introduction to Global Development Studies
courses.description: Introduces competing ideas of development and the institutions that pursue them. Class meetings are mostly discussion, and writing assignments move from brief responses to a longer paper.

descriptions.CSC-105: Looks at how computing shapes work, privacy, creativity and public life. Students experiment with the underlying technologies and write about their social effects; no programming background is expected.
descriptions.CSC-151: A first course in computer science that teaches problem solving through functional programming. Students work in pairs on daily labs, building programs from small functions and learning to reason about recursion and data.
descriptions.CSC-161: Continues the introductory sequence with imperative programming in a low-level language. Labs cover memory, pointers, arrays and linked structures, along with the tools programmers use to build and test software.
descriptions.CSC-205: Introduces computational approaches to human language, including parsing, language models and the evaluation of language technologies. Students build small systems and consider what they do and do not capture about language.
descriptions.CSC-207: Develops object-oriented design alongside the core data structures and algorithms of computer science. Students implement lists, trees, hash tables and graphs and analyze their running time.
descriptions.CSC-208: Covers the mathematics that computer science depends on: logic, proof, sets, relations, counting and graphs. Students practice writing rigorous arguments and connect each topic to programs.
descriptions.CSC-211: Explains how a computer executes a program, from digital logic and machine instructions up to the processor and memory hierarchy. Students design simple hardware components and write assembly code.
descriptions.CSC-213: Studies how operating systems manage processes, memory and files, and how programs can run correctly in parallel. Labs involve building pieces of a system and writing concurrent code.
descriptions.CSC-214: A half-semester introduction to how computer systems and networks are attacked and defended. Students study common vulnerabilities, basic cryptography and the practice of secure design.
descriptions.CSC-216: A half-semester introduction to how computers communicate, from local links to the global internet. Students examine the layered protocols and write simple networked programs.
descriptions.CSC-232: A half-semester introduction to designing technology around the people who use it. Students observe users, prototype interfaces and evaluate them.
